text.p: * Partial results in the run-off to presidential elections confirmed exit polls showing that opposition candidate Emil Constantinescu defeated President Ion Iliescu.

* The Central Electoral Bureau (BEC) released data gathered from 80.3 percent of polling stations, showing Constantinescu got 55.15 percent of votes while Iliescu got 44.85 percent. Turnout of Sunday's second round was 75.83 percent.
* The BEC is expected to release results of further vote counting at 1530.
* Romania has finally achieved its "velvet revolution" very similar with the one in Czechoslovakia in 1989, National Peasant Party secretary general Radu Vasile told a news conference.

* A parallel vote count by the Democratic Convention (CDR) showed that only some 11.3 percent of votes for Constantinescu came from the Social Democratic Union (USD), while nine percent came from the country's ethnic Hungarians, Radu Vasile said.
Vasile said these percentages raised the possibility that the Hungrarian Democratic Union (UDMR) could become part of Romania's new ruling coalition.
He said the UDMR was likely to get some positions in the economic ministries, but not jobs as local prefects.

* France's ambassador to Romania, Bernard Boyer, read a message from President Jacques Chirac, saying the Constantinescu's victory on Sunday proved Romania's bid for European integration and opened the perspective of a new bilateral cooperation with France.
* Constantinescu pledged in interview to allow only competence and morality as criteria for promotion and ban any political cleansing or revenge.
He said the change of power in Romania has already registered very positive reactions from abroad.
* Constantinescu said the CDR's coalition agreement with the USD was not aimed at negotiating portfolios, but ellaborating a coherent governing programme.
* Romanian-Russian relations are a priority for whoever is Romania's president, Constantinescu said. These relations should be freed from the history's dark moments.
He said a political treaty with Russia was needed to build reconciliation and the basis of future cooperation.
He said the reconciliation should come from parties which do not have a communist past.
He said the former Soviet Union should not be entirely blamed for transforming Romania into a communist country after the World War Two.
Constantinescu hoped he could play a key role in in bringing Russian-Romanian relations back to normal. He said he had no prejudices against Russians. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
